implementationPlan.description: TDD RED in the real Web-standard HTTP adapter lifecycle suite. Add a batch-body helper and a nonzero two-case matrix for duplicate numeric and duplicate string ids; each POST must settle promptly as HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error.code -32602, error.data.code INPUT_INVALID, id null, and zero authenticate/dispatch calls. Prove the refusal leaves no stale in-flight id by immediately sending a fresh distinct batch reusing that id. ARMS ADDED (all in the real Web-standard adapter lifecycle suite, no mocked transport):
1. Duplicate matrix, denominator 4 — DUPLICATE_ID_CASES = [7, "request-7", 0, ""]. Nonzero-case guards assert length > 0 AND that both a numeric and a string case exist, so a silently emptied or single-type sweep cannot pass. Per case: HTTP 400, payload id null, error.code -32602, error.data.code INPUT_INVALID, port.calls [] and port.dispatched [] (zero authenticate AND zero dispatch). No-stale-id proof rides in the same loop: immediately after each refusal the SAME id paired with FRESH_PARTNER_ID is POSTed and must return 200 with two correlated results and dispatched.length 2 — a screen that registered before validating would refuse this.
2. Cross-POST batch overlap — deferred batch [21,22] in flight, second batch [23,22] refuses -32602/INPUT_INVALID, port.calls stays at exactly two dispatches so the FRESH id 23 never ran either, then release and the first batch correlates BOTH ids 21 and 22.
3. Positive controls, new describe "batch shapes the duplicate-id screen must not refuse": distinct ids [31,"thirty-two"] -> 200, one correlated response per id, 2 dispatches; two id-less notifications -> HTTP 202 with empty body and zero dispatch; two explicit id:null messages -> the SDK's own -32700 with error.data undefined and zero dispatch, asserting it is NOT the adapter's -32602/INPUT_INVALID (task rail: null ids are not correlated request ids).

All three controls and the cross-POST arm were GREEN at red time, so they pin existing behavior rather than the fix.

Helpers added: batchBody, toolCall, readBatchPayload (a batch answers with a JSON-RPC array, which readPayload's single-object shape cannot hold), byJsonText total order so arrival order is not asserted, and settlesWithin(label, promise) with a 2000ms budget — an unscreened duplicate leaves one response pending until session close, so an unbounded await would hang the file instead of failing the named arm. That bound is what makes the step-5 mutation drill produce an attributable red.

implementationPlan.description: Extract the bounded-body, loopback, JSON-RPC shape/id, and stable response helpers from http-server.ts into new focused production module packages/mcp/src/http/http-request-screen.ts so both production files finish below their caps. Preserve existing behavior byte-for-byte for errorResponse/refusalResponse, loopbackRefusal, readBoundedBody, and isInitializePayload. Add `screenRequestIds(value, inflight)` that scans method-bearing numeric/string ids once with a local Set; return a frozen accepted distinct-id list only after the whole body proves unique and disjoint from the session's existing set, otherwise return a frozen refusal marker. Do not add to or delete from the caller's set inside this pure screen.
implementationPlan.note:
Extracted the pre-dispatch screening responsibility into new production module packages/mcp/src/http/http-request-screen.ts (194 physical lines, under the 250 target). Moved verbatim, no behavioural edit: LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES, errorResponse, refusalResponse, LOOPBACK_AUTHORITY_PATTERN/isLoopbackAuthority, loopbackRefusal, limitRefusal, BoundedBody, readCappedBytes, readBoundedBody, isInitializePayload. requestIdsOf deliberately LEFT in http-server.ts for now — step 4 is where it is replaced by the new screen, so this step stays a pure move.

NEW SURFACE: `screenRequestIds(value, inflight: ReadonlySet<number|string>): RequestIdScreen`. Single pass, local `seen` Set; a message is correlatable only when it carries BOTH a string method and a number|string id, so responses (no method), id-less notifications and explicit `id: null` are skipped and cannot collide. `1` and `"1"` stay distinct because Set membership compares the values as themselves. Refusal returns the module-level frozen `REQUEST_IDS_REFUSED` ({ok:false}) which has NO `accepted` member at all, so there is no shape in which a caller can read ids out of a refusal; acceptance freezes both the verdict and the distinct-id array, and is built only AFTER the whole body has scanned clean. `inflight` is typed ReadonlySet, so "does not add to or delete from the caller's set" is enforced by the compiler rather than promised in a comment.

http-server.ts now imports errorResponse/isInitializePayload/loopbackRefusal/readBoundedBody/refusalResponse from ./http-request-screen.js and re-exports LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES from it (same idiom as the existing HTTP_LISTED_TOOLS re-export), so the module's public surface is unchanged and mcp-root-surface.test.ts's WITHHELD_HTTP_VALUES negative control is untouched. Dropped the now-unused MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES value import and RuntimeError type import from http-server.ts (TS6133/TS6196 caught this; both now live in the screen module).

SEAM, http-server.ts:302-305 — the whole change:
  const screenedIds = screenRequestIds(body.value, inflightRequestIds);
  if (!screenedIds.ok) return refusalResponse("INPUT_INVALID");

ORDERING, read off the delivered file rather than asserted in prose: the refusal `return` at :303 sits ABOVE every side effect. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the existing INPUT_INVALID transport refusal (HTTP 400, JSON-RPC -32602, runtime code INPUT_INVALID) for both within-batch and cross-POST correlation conflicts; rejected inventing a new runtime error or hand-built -32600 row because that would widen the contracts registry for a transport-local safety check and lose the existing stable evidence. Extract the whole HTTP request-screening responsibility rather than adding five lines in place: http-server.ts is already 501 lines, so touching it without a real split would violate the repository's split-before-400 rail. Rejected post-dispatch deduplication because the SDK stream map is already overwritten by then.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Current HEAD 27c53ee contains prior fix 5f9772e: packages/mcp/src/http/http-server.ts requestIdsOf collects every method-bearing numeric/string id, checks only attachment.inflightRequestIds, then inserts ids into the set before SDK dispatch. A duplicate id appearing twice in one decoded batch therefore passes the `some(inflight.has)` check and both messages dispatch. Candidate production/test paths are clean. Live probe confirmed distinct request ids return HTTP 200 with a two-element correlated response array and two dispatches; two notifications with omitted ids return HTTP 202 and zero dispatch; explicit id:null messages reach the SDK and retain its HTTP 400 JSON-RPC parse error with zero dispatch. Existing cross-POST protection and lifecycle tests live in http-server-lifecycle.test.ts.
planningNotes.risks: The guard must compare numeric ids as numbers and string ids as strings (1 and '1' remain distinct), ignore messages without a correlatable numeric/string id, and validate the entire decoded batch before adding any id to the attachment set. Do not mutate inflightRequestIds until screening succeeds. Ensure the existing settle path releases every distinct accepted id, while a refused local duplicate adds none. Preserve the SDK's notification/id:null behavior rather than interpreting null as a request id. The mutation drill can make the duplicate request hang in the SDK; keep the focused integration assertion timeout-bounded and restore the new untracked module via temp SHA256 proof.
